transcript.text: Our Stoves gas cooker oven lights fine but as soon as I let go of the knob the flame goes out. Hob burners all fine. It's a Richmond something, freestanding. Is this a DIY job?

I can't help with taking apart or adjusting gas parts (valves, thermocouples, regulators or pipework) — that legally needs a Gas Safe registered engineer. Probably not a DIY repair. A gas oven that lights but dies as the knob is released most often has a flame-failure device (usually its thermocouple/flame sensor) that is not detecting the flame, so it safely shuts the gas off. The fact the hob burners work makes a general gas-supply issue less likely. 1. Try lighting it normally and keep the oven control pressed in for 10–15 seconds after the flame appears, then release it. If it stays lit, it may simply have needed a little longer for the safety sensor to warm up.
2. If it still goes out, with the cooker fully cool and isolated, only inspect what is visible around the oven burner for obvious food debris, grease or moisture. Do not dismantle the burner or touch gas connections. A dirty or poorly directed flame can fail to heat the sensor properly. If it continues to go out after the longer hold, arrange a Gas Safe registered cooker engineer. They can check the thermocouple/flame-failure device, its positioning and the oven gas valve safely. Do not bypass or hold the control in during use; that safety device is there to prevent unburnt gas escaping.

Thanks. I've tried holding it in for 15, 20 and even 30 seconds and it still goes out. There's some burnt-on fat around the base of the burner near the probe. Only smell gas briefly while lighting, and my CO alarm hasn't sounded. Should I get an engineer in?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
If you can smell gas, treat it as an emergency: don't turn any switches on or off and no naked flames. Turn the gas off at the meter if you safely can, open doors and windows, and leave if the smell is strong. Call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999.

candidates: Oven flame-failure device / thermocouple not proving the flame (high)
Oven burner flame not heating the sensor properly due to dirt, moisture or burner alignment (medium)

reading.symptom: Oven flame goes out when the knob is released

tags.checkGiven: Now try lighting it again as normal. Does it light and stay lit now, or still not?

plan: They asked: "Is this a DIY job?" - answer that first.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Stoves.
The fault they reported is: "Oven flame goes out when the knob is released". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.
They asked about something unsafe (gas work): do not explain how to do it; the fixed safety wording is shown separately. Offer the safe alternative.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

hazards.clause: only smell gas briefly while lighting
